title: [CQ-M03b] maintenance workload fixtures
description: Objective: Freeze five distinct maintenance workloads for the 20-case CQ-M03 matched corpus. Deliverable: packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/maintenanceWorkloads.ts and maintenanceWorkloads.test.ts, exporting this category's frozen dataset using the M03a workloadSnapshot contract. Frozen corpus contract (version 1): each workload has a unique category-prefixed id, category (maintenance/defect/refactor/non-routine), full startingCommit 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71, named repo source provenance, intendedBehavior/task instructions, deterministic snapshot digest over a documented sorted-path/UTF-8-byte encoding, initialFiles and separately held-out assessmentFiles (relative portable paths mapped to immutable UTF-8 strings), and explicit assessment rubric criteria/coverage tags. assessmentFiles contains executable independent black-box acceptance tests; it must not be copied into the coding snapshot. Include bounded reviewable Node ESM fixture source adaptations grounded in original Moe source, not twenty renamed toy cases, and label any reduced/adapted snapshot provenance honestly. No reference solution in coding inputs. Every case has a concrete original-state failure/required change and unchanged-acceptance positive and adversarial-negative controls; no agent judge/price/network dependency. The shared materializer owns only newly created os.tmpdir directories and offers fresh reset by new snapshot creation, never an arbitrary target root or Git reset/worktree operation. Category boundary: Five cases: integrate an already-present UTF-8 truncation helper instead of duplicating it (reusable-helper tag); update literal/glob branch-policy messaging without changing match semantics; retain unknown token values when updating human-readable usage formatting; add a caller that reuses affected-file normalization with Windows/Unicode paths; update a cached-ref lookup recipe for a changed caller without changing protected-branch intent. Ground provenance in util/memorySettings.ts, util/branchPolicy.ts, scripts/prompt-cache-usage.mjs, util/affectedFiles.ts and util/cachedPlanPaths.ts. Each intended maintenance change has an observable black-box criterion plus compatibility examples. Keep all fixture payloads/test-only corrected and plausible-wrong variants in these two files; no production edits, benchmark runs, aggregate corpus edits or edits to the dependency. Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/benchmarks/maintenanceWorkloads.test.ts
definitionOfDone: Exactly five distinct maintenance fixtures validate against landed M03a contract, with frozen full starting commit, source provenance, intended behavior, content hashes and independent executable acceptance rubrics.

Each fixture has an unsolved original that fails at least one intended-change criterion, a test-only corrected variant passing the same unchanged rubric, and a plausible wrong variant rejected by it; no reference solution or assessment bytes enter coding inputs.

Cases retain category-specific invariants and explicit context/helper/caller/requirements/recipe coverage tags where applicable; snapshots and repeated resets are deterministic and never alter source checkout bytes.
Fresh cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/benchmarks/maintenanceWorkloads.test.ts exits 0 with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits or Git-write commands; wrappers own landing. Preserve all peer/pre-existing dirty bytes.
Frozen benchmark/test scaffolding only; do not alter production behavior, enable verified-local, or claim VM/isolation certification.
Do not edit sibling category datasets/tests, the shared contract after it lands, or the M03 assembler; use explicit dependency updates for any contract change.

implementationPlan.description:
Prerequisites + harness (TDD red). First confirm CQ-M03a (task-44b44ccac62f4657890f98ff450738c8) is DONE/landed and READ its landed packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/workloadSnapshot.ts; this plan uses its planned names (validateWorkloads, digestFiles, digestWorkload, createCodingSnapshot, createAssessmentSnapshot, readSnapshotFiles, WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV, FROZEN_STARTING_COMMIT, SOURCE_REPOSITORY, CORPUS_COVERAGE_TAGS), so adapt to the actual exports and NEVER edit that contract (if it blocks a fixture, stop and use moe.report_blocked / an explicit dependency update). Read the grounding sources at the frozen commit, read-only: `git show 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71:<path>` for packages/moe-daemon/src/util/{memorySettings,branchPolicy,affectedFiles,cachedPlanPaths}.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getPendingQuestions.ts and scripts/prompt-cache-usage.mjs (the dirty working-tree copies differ only by CRLF). Create packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/maintenanceWorkloads.test.ts (vitest, LF) importing `MAINTENANCE_WORKLOADS` from './maintenanceWorkloads.js' (red: the module does not exist yet) and the M03a API. Build:
(a) dataset tests: validateWorkloads(MAINTENANCE_WORKLOADS) succeeds; exactly the five pinned ids in order ['maintenance-truncation-helper-reuse','maintenance-branch-policy-message','maintenance-usage-unknown-format','maintenance-affected-file-caller','maintenance-cached-ref-caller']; every category 'maintenance'; startingCommit === FROZEN_STARTING_COMMIT; each source.paths entry is one of the grounding paths above, adaptation is 'reduced' or 'adapted' with an honest note; coverage tags include 'reusable-helper' on case 1 and 'changed-caller' on case 5; per-case digestWorkload literals (pinned in step 3).
(b) one shared control harness: runAssessment(workload, candidateRoot) creates an assessment snapshot and runs `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--test', '--test-reporter=tap', ...each *.test.mjs path], { cwd: assessmentRoot, env: { ...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: '', [WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV]: candidateRoot }, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 60000 })`, then parses `ok N - <name>` / `not ok N - <name>` lines into passed/failed criterion ids. Assessment test names must start with `<criterion-id>: `. Error handling: a spawn error, signal or timeout is reported as a failure with a bounded output excerpt, never as a pass. Variants are applied by writing their bytes into a FRESH coding snapshot root (test-only; never into the dataset).
(c) generic per-case control test (it.each over a table of { id, corrected: files, wrong: files, wrongMustFail: criterionId }): the original fails with status != 0 and at least one intended-change criterion in failed; the corrected variant exits 0 with EVERY rubric criterion id in passed (so each criterion really executed); the plausible-wrong variant exits != 0 with wrongMustFail in failed (it fails for the intended reason, not a crash).
(d) leakage: no initial file contains or equals any assessment file or corrected/wrong variant file content, and no coding snapshot contains a *.test.mjs file.
(e) determinism and reset: two coding snapshots read back identically with digest === snapshotDigest; after mutating one, a new snapshot restores the frozen digest.
(f) source checkout untouched: sha256 of the dataset module and the six grounding files is identical before and after the suite.
Dispose every handle in afterEach. Give the control tests a 120s timeout.

Cases 1-2: create packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/maintenanceWorkloads.ts exporting `MAINTENANCE_WORKLOADS = validateWorkloads([...])` (validated and frozen at import; the dataset module holds ONLY workload objects - corrected and plausible-wrong variants live in the test file). Fixture code is bounded Node ESM .mjs adapted from the grounding source (types removed, behaviour kept); assessment files are self-contained node:test + node:assert + node:fs/path/url, and import candidate modules via pathToFileURL(path.join(process.env[WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV], ...)), failing loudly if the env var is unset.
CASE 1 'maintenance-truncation-helper-reuse' (tags reusable-helper, utf8-boundary; source memorySettings.ts + tools/getPendingQuestions.ts, adapted). initialFiles: src/textBudget.mjs = truncateForBudget adapted to never split a surrogate pair (note says so), and src/compactQuestion.mjs = compactQuestion adapted from getPendingQuestions, but in the ORIGINAL it truncates by itself with a naive content.slice(0, max) and no flags. intendedBehavior: over-budget content must use the existing helper and return { ...question, content, contentTruncated: true, contentOriginalLength }; within budget or max <= 0 returns the same object; never duplicate truncation logic. Criteria: returns-compact-shape (exact fields, ends with the ellipsis, length <= max); keeps-complete-characters (emoji at the cut is not split, no lone surrogate); passes-short-through (toBe the input); reuses-text-budget-helper (static: compactQuestion.mjs imports truncateForBudget from './textBudget.mjs' and contains no .slice(/.substring(/ellipsis literal of its own); helper-unchanged (textBudget compatibility table). Test-only corrected: imports and uses the helper. Plausible-wrong: an inline copy of the helper code (behaviour correct) -> wrongMustFail 'reuses-text-budget-helper'.
CASE 2 'maintenance-branch-policy-message' (tags message-update, compatibility; source branchPolicy.ts, adapted). initialFiles: src/branchPolicy.mjs with matchesBranchPattern and describeBranchPolicyFailure as at the frozen commit. intendedBehavior: the failure message must name the policy kind - a literal pattern says `requires branch "<pattern>"`, a glob (contains *) says `requires a branch matching "<pattern>"` - keeping the completed-branch clause and the remediation sentence verbatim, with match semantics unchanged. Criteria: literal-policy-message and glob-policy-message (exact full strings); keeps-remediation; match-semantics-unchanged (table: literal equal/case-different, 'moe/work-*' on a dated branch, 'release/v1.0-*' must NOT match 'release/v1X0-a' but must match 'release/v1.0-a', literal 'feature/(x)', '**' collapsing, anchoring, empty, a 256-char branch, 11 wildcards, non-strings -> false). Corrected: branches only the message on pattern.includes('*'). Plausible-wrong: also 'simplifies' the matcher to an unescaped replace of * with .* -> wrongMustFail 'match-semantics-unchanged'.
Pin each workload's snapshotDigest/assessmentDigest from digestFiles. Run only `npx vitest run src/benchmarks/maintenanceWorkloads.test.ts` in the isolated Linux copy; cases 1-2 controls green.

Cases 3-5 in the same two files, then freeze. CASE 3 'maintenance-usage-unknown-format' (tags unknown-preservation, format-update, compatibility; source scripts/prompt-cache-usage.mjs, reduced: count/counter/sum, normalizeUsage and formatUsage only). intendedBehavior: new line format `[prompt-cache] provider=

input= cached= written= uncached= hit= output= reasoning= total=`. When input accounting is incomplete, input/cached/written/uncached/hit are each the literal `unknown` (replacing the single usage=unknown token) while output/reasoning/total keep their own values. A missing or invalid counter is never shown as 0; codex has written=unknown; a zero total gives hit=n/a; normalizeUsage is unchanged. Criteria: claude-complete-line (exact string for input 10/read 30/write 60/output 7 -> input=100 cached=30 written=60 uncached=10 hit=30.0% output=7 reasoning=unknown total=107); codex-complete-line (exact string with reasoning); unknown-input-fields; unknown-output-fields (missing output, inconsistent reasoning); zero-total-hit; normalize-unchanged (table incl. codex read>input -> cacheReadTokens null). Corrected: the new format with ?? 'unknown'. Plausible-wrong: the new format but `?? 0` defaults -> wrongMustFail 'unknown-input-fields'. CASE 4 'maintenance-affected-file-caller' (tags reusable-helper, new-caller, windows-paths, unicode-paths; source affectedFiles.ts, adapted). initialFiles: src/affectedFiles.mjs = normalizeAffectedFile, normalizeAffectedFiles and pathKey adapted to take an explicit platform argument (deterministic on every OS; note says so), plus src/declaredFiles.mjs whose mergeDeclaredFiles(existing, incoming, platform) throws 'not implemented'. intendedBehavior: append newly declared paths normalized by the shared normalizer, dedupe by pathKey(p, platform) keeping the first spelling and order, preserve Unicode spelling exactly, and let the normalizer's traversal/absolute error propagate without mutating `existing`. Criteria: windows-separators (multiple backslashes, leading ./); platform-case-folding (win32/darwin fold 'Src/A.ts' with 'src/a.ts' and 'DOCS/CAF\u00c9.md' with 'docs/caf\u00e9.md'; linux keeps both); unicode-preserved; rejects-traversal (normalizer message, input arrays unchanged); reuses-normalizer (static: imports from './affectedFiles.mjs', no own backslash replace or toLowerCase); normalizer-unchanged. Corrected: reuses both helpers. Plausible-wrong: own p.replace('\\','/') (first match only) plus an unconditional toLowerCase -> wrongMustFail 'windows-separators'. CASE 5 'maintenance-cached-ref-caller' (tags changed-caller, protected-branch-intent, read-only-recipe; source cachedPlanPaths.ts, reduced: cachedPlanRef plus findCachedPlanPaths with an injected runner, the realpath/toplevel/budget parts dropped, as the note says). initialFiles also hold src/submitPlanLookup.mjs, the CHANGED caller, which now passes `{ branch, remote }` so the original lookup always misses. intendedBehavior: accept { branch, remote = 'origin' } (and still the legacy string) and resolve refs/remotes//. Only a literal branch is evidence (same cachedPlanRef rules); remote must be one safe component, else miss before any git call. The recipe stays exactly config --local --includes --get-regexp, rev-parse --verify --end-of-options ^{commit}, --literal-pathspecs ls-tree -z --full-tree -- , with no fetch/for-each-ref/ls-remote/checkout. Criteria: accepts-caller-options, legacy-string-still-works, glob-is-not-evidence (miss, zero runner calls), rejects-unsafe-remote ('origin/../heads', '*', '-x', '', 'a.lock'), read-only-recipe (exact recorded argv via a fake runner). Corrected: options support plus remote validation. Plausible-wrong: resolves a glob branch through `for-each-ref` -> wrongMustFail 'glob-is-not-evidence'. Freeze: pin snapshotDigest/assessmentDigest in each workload and the five digestWorkload literals in the test. Make the whole file green in the isolated Linux copy (focused runs only).

The one verification gate. Build a FRESH synchronized isolated copy (recipe in planningNotes; it must contain the landed M03a contract), add the two owned files' working-tree bytes, and with Linux-only PATH run exactly: `cd <copy>/packages/moe-daemon && PATH=/home/sysadmin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin npx vitest run src/benchmarks/maintenanceWorkloads.test.ts` (fresh exit 0; report actual pass/skip counts). Then run `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` with the same PATH (the dataset is under src/ and compiles into dist; vitest does not typecheck). Run the focused file a second time to show the controls are repeatable, and confirm no `moe-workload-*` temp dirs are left behind. Never touch the original Windows node_modules or any package-lock.json, and confirm the two tested files are byte-identical (sha256) to the working tree. Keep the command and output tail for complete_task.

Exactly one adversarial self-review of the two-file diff (load adversarial-self-review). Challenge each case. Does the original really fail an intended-change criterion, and not just crash? Does the corrected variant pass EVERY criterion and the wrong variant fail the named one? Could a no-op or a solution that only rewrites the tests pass? Are the static reuse checks too loose (an aliased import) or too strict (formatting)? Is the solution, an assessment file or a variant leaking into initialFiles, intendedBehavior or the dataset module? Are provenance labels honest (reduced/adapted notes match what changed)? Are template-literal escapes right (backslashes, backticks and `${` inside fixture code), and are digests pinned and stable on CRLF checkouts (template literals normalize line endings)? Do any criteria depend on the platform, clock, network, locale or a real git? Is os.tmpdir() left clean and the source checkout unchanged? Confirm: no edit to workloadSnapshot.ts or sibling datasets, no production/daemon change, no Git or .moe writes, no benchmark results or VM/readiness claims. Also confirm no substring from the project's global forbiddenPatterns (project.globalRails) appears anywhere in the two files, fixture strings included; a substring match also fires inside longer identifiers. Fix findings with tests; if any byte changed after step 4, rerun the step-4 commands fresh and use that output for complete_task.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- **Five cases, each with an independent black-box rubric.** Each case has two kinds of rubric criteria. Behaviour criteria import the candidate's .mjs by file URL. Structural criteria are static source checks, used only where the task is about reuse (cases 1 and 4).
- **Rejected: judging by an agent or by text similarity.** Neither is executable or reproducible.
- **Rejected: storing corrected solutions in the dataset module.** M04 imports the dataset, so solutions would leak into coding inputs. Variants live only in the test file.
- **Shared control harness (one per test file).** Each assessment runs through `node --test --test-reporter=tap`, and the harness parses TAP. This proves three things against the same unchanged rubric:
  - the original fails a NAMED intended-change criterion;
  - the corrected variant passes every criterion;
  - the plausible-wrong variant fails the specific criterion it was designed to break.
- **Real git is never used.** Case 5 injects a fake runner and records argv, so the suite works without .git and offline.
- **pathKey takes an explicit platform argument (case 4).** That makes win32/darwin/linux folding testable on any host, and the fixture note discloses the adaptation.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- **Grounding files at the frozen commit:**
  - memorySettings.ts has only truncateForBudget. Its callers are getPendingQuestions.compactQuestion, chatPayload and taskPayload.
  - branchPolicy.ts has matchesBranchPattern (escape-then-expand, `**` collapse, length/wildcard caps) and describeBranchPolicyFailure.
  - prompt-cache-usage.mjs has normalizeUsage and formatUsage (missing counters are 'unknown'; codex read>input means unknown).
  - affectedFiles.ts has normalizeAffectedFile (backslashes to '/', strips './', rejects traversal/absolute) and a platform-dependent pathKey.
  - cachedPlanPaths.ts has cachedPlanRef (literal-only refs/remotes/origin/<branch>) and findCachedPlanPaths. The latter has an injectable runner, a config/promisor refusal, rev-parse --verify --end-of-options, and ls-tree --literal-pathspecs.
  - The working-tree copies of these files are dirty with CRLF churn only. Read them through `git show 35cf53c:<path>`.
- **Unicode matters:** ECMAScript template literals normalize CRLF/CR to LF, so fixture bytes and digests do not depend on how the .ts file is checked out.
- **M03a's planned contract:** exact workload keys, criterion ids that must appear in *.test.mjs assessments, MOE_WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV, and fresh mkdtemp snapshots with WeakMap-owned dispose. Read the landed version first.
- **Naming convention:** category datasets export `<CATEGORY>_WORKLOADS` (MAINTENANCE_WORKLOADS here) so the M03 assembler imports one name per category.
- **Isolated Linux copy recipe:**
  1. `D=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-m03b-test.XXXXXX)`
  2. `git -C /mnt/d/projexts/moes archive HEAD packages/moe-daemon docs scripts CLAUDE.md .gitignore package.json | tar -x -C "$D"`
  3. Copy the owned files' working-tree bytes into the copy.
  4. `ln -s "$(cat /tmp/moe-linux-test-root.latest)/repo/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules" "$D/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules"`
  5. Run with PATH=/home/sysadmin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin.
  Re-copy before each focused run, and never run vitest against the shared tree's Windows node_modules.
planningNotes.risks:
- **Vacuous controls:** require the wrong variant to fail the NAMED criterion, and the corrected variant to report every criterion id as `ok`. A crash or syntax error must not count as a correct rejection.
- **Template-literal escaping:** fixture JS containing backslashes, backticks or `${` must be escaped in the .ts literals (`\\`, a backslash before each backtick, `\${`). Prefer string concatenation inside fixture code. Execution of the controls catches mistakes.
- **Forbidden patterns:** the project's global forbiddenPatterns (project.globalRails) are substring checks and apply to fixture strings too. That includes the dunder-proto token, the markup-injection DOM property, and the dynamic-code call token. The last one also fires inside any longer identifier ending in those four letters plus an open parenthesis, so avoid such identifiers.
- **Static reuse checks:** keep them tolerant of formatting and quote style, but strict on the required import source and on duplicated logic.
- **Node version:** `--test-reporter=tap` needs Node 18.15+, which the Linux Node 24 and CI provide. Pass NODE_OPTIONS='' and a timeout to every spawn.
- **Dependency:** M03a is unlanded at planning time. Do not start until its task is DONE, and adapt to its real exports without editing it.
- **Honest provenance:** every fixture is a reduced/adapted ESM copy at commit 35cf53c, never a whole-repository snapshot. Notes must say exactly what was dropped or changed.
- **Repo hygiene:** no production edits, no Git/.moe writes, and preserve the shared tree's peer/pre-existing dirty bytes. Iterate with focused runs only.
